title: Sobur Review: Does It Work? DHM Dose, Ingredients and Value
excerpt: An honest Sobur review: what's in these DHM hangover pills, how its 300 mg DHM dose compares with other brands, side effects, value, and who should skip it.
metaDescription: Honest Sobur review: what's in these DHM hangover pills, how 300 mg compares with other brands, side effects, value, and who should skip it.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**The honest verdict first:** Sobur is a small, long-running capsule hangover supplement built around DHM (dihydromyricetin, a plant compound from the Japanese raisin tree), with N-acetyl compounds, vitamin C, and B vitamins added. The formula is sensible and short, which we like. The weak spots are the dose and the marketing. Sobur's own listing advertises 300 mg of DHM, which is low next to the 600 to 1,000 mg that most standalone DHM products give you per serving, and the brand calls itself a "hangover cure" and its ingredients "clinically proven," which the research does not support. No independent clinical trial has tested Sobur itself.

**Who it suits:** occasional social drinkers who want a simple DHM-plus-vitamins product and don't mind paying more per milligram of DHM. **Who should skip it:** people who mainly want DHM at a meaningful dose (a plain DHM product gives you two to three times as much for less money), anyone on prescription medicines who hasn't checked with a pharmacist, and anyone drinking heavily or often, which no supplement fixes.

> **This is not medical advice.** This review explains published research, the brand's own descriptions, and general supplement science. It is not a substitute for a doctor or pharmacist who knows your health history. Sobur is a dietary supplement, not a drug. It has not been approved by the FDA to prevent or treat hangovers, and it does not lower your blood alcohol, sober you up, or make it safe to drive. **Ask a doctor or pharmacist first if** you take prescription medicine (especially blood thinners, sedatives, sleep aids, anxiety medication, or diabetes medicines), are pregnant or breastfeeding, or have liver or kidney disease. If someone shows signs of alcohol poisoning, such as confusion, vomiting while drowsy, slow or irregular breathing, or can't be woken up, call 911.

**About our relationship with Sobur:** we don't have an affiliate arrangement with Sobur, so this review doesn't link to its store and we earn nothing if you buy it. We do earn a commission on two plain DHM products mentioned near the end, and we say so where they appear.

## What Sobur Is

Sobur is a hangover supplement sold as capsules, mainly through the brand's own website and, at various times, through Amazon and overseas marketplaces. The site lists the company as Fortius Labs LTD, with a mailing address in California and a link to a Finnish version of the site, so it's a small international operation rather than a big consumer-health company. The brand has been around for years, which makes it one of the older names in the DHM category.

The pitch is straightforward. Sobur says its pills help your body process alcohol faster, protect your liver, and bring brain chemistry back to normal after drinking, so you wake up feeling better. The suggested use is one to two capsules before bed with plenty of water. Bottles are sold in small counts (20-capsule bottles are the common listing), which means a bottle covers somewhere between 10 and 20 nights depending on whether you take one capsule or two.

The site also includes the standard supplement disclaimer that the product "is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease." That line sits a little awkwardly next to the brand's own headline describing Sobur as a hangover cure. We'll come back to that.

## What's in Sobur Hangover Pills

Sobur's formula is short compared with "kitchen sink" products that pack in 20 or more ingredients. Based on the brand's descriptions and its marketplace listings, the main ingredients are:

- **DHM (dihydromyricetin).** Also called ampelopsin and sold as Hovenia dulcis (Japanese raisin tree) extract. This is the headline ingredient. Sobur's long-running Amazon listing advertises 300 mg of DHM.
- **An N-acetyl compound labeled "NAC."** Most hangover formulas that list NAC mean N-acetyl cysteine, an amino acid your body uses to make glutathione, its main built-in antioxidant. Sobur's own site spells it out in one place as "N-Acetyl L-Carnitine," which is a different compound (acetyl-L-carnitine). That looks like a labeling slip, but it's worth checking the Supplement Facts panel on the bottle you actually buy so you know which one you're getting.
- **Vitamin C.** Pitched as an antioxidant.
- **B vitamins.** Marketplace listings mention niacin, B5, B6, and B12. Alcohol use can lower some B vitamin levels, which is the usual reason they appear in hangover products.

The brand also says the capsules are made in the USA in a cGMP-certified facility. cGMP means "current good manufacturing practice," the FDA's baseline rules for how supplements are made and labeled. It's a minimum standard, not a sign of extra testing. We didn't find published third-party testing results for Sobur, such as a certificate of analysis showing measured DHM content, so treat the label amounts as the brand's claim.

One honest caution: we couldn't find a single, consistent milligram breakdown for every ingredient across the brand's pages, and supplement formulas get reworked over time. We're not going to invent figures. If exact amounts matter to you, and they should if you take other medicines, read the panel on the bottle in front of you.

## The DHM Dose: Sobur vs Standalone DHM

This is the part most Sobur reviews skip, and it's the most useful thing to know before buying.

The headline 300 mg figure is low for a product built around DHM. For comparison, most of the plain DHM products we've reviewed provide around 1,000 mg per serving, and DHM-focused blends such as Cheers Restore sit in the several-hundred-milligram range. Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) covers why there's no official dose for hangovers, but the amounts people commonly use fall roughly between 300 and 1,200 mg, often scaled to how much they plan to drink. At 300 mg you're at the bottom of that range.

There's a wrinkle worth noting. The listing advertises 300 mg, but the directions say one to two capsules. If the 300 mg refers to one capsule, two capsules gets you to about 600 mg, which is more reasonable but uses up the bottle twice as fast. If it refers to the full suggested serving, you're getting 300 mg no matter what. Check the Supplement Facts panel: it will say "Serving size: 1 capsule" or "Serving size: 2 capsules," and the DHM amount listed is per serving.

Either way, the math tends to come out the same. Take the price of the bottle, divide by the number of servings, then divide by how much DHM is in each serving. A plain 1,000 mg DHM product almost always wins on DHM per dollar, often by a wide margin. What you get with Sobur in exchange is the added NAC, vitamin C, and B vitamins in the same capsule.

## Does Sobur Work? What the Evidence Says

No published clinical trial has tested Sobur as a finished product. So the fair question is what the evidence says about its ingredients, at roughly the doses it uses.

### DHM: interesting science, mostly in animals

The best-known DHM research is a 2012 study by Jing Liang and colleagues at UCLA, published in the *Journal of Neuroscience*. In rats, DHM reduced signs of alcohol intoxication and withdrawal, and it appears to work partly by counteracting alcohol's effects on GABA-A receptors, the brain's main "calm down" signaling system. Sobur's site quotes Liang from a 2012 *New Scientist* article about that work. Other lab and animal studies suggest DHM may support the enzymes that break down alcohol and its toxic byproduct, acetaldehyde, and may reduce some liver stress markers.

The catch is that strong human evidence is thin. There's no good evidence from large, independent human trials that DHM prevents hangovers, and the human studies that exist are small. DHM is also poorly absorbed from the gut, which is part of why products use larger doses. Our [honest DHM science review](/never-hungover/does-dhm-work-honest-science-review-2025) goes through the studies in more detail.

### NAC: plausible, with limited human data

If the "NAC" in Sobur is N-acetyl cysteine, the reasoning is that it feeds glutathione, which helps clear acetaldehyde. That's biologically sensible, and hospitals use high-dose NAC for a very different purpose (acetaminophen overdose). For hangovers specifically, the human evidence is limited to small studies with mixed results. Our [NAC and alcohol guide](/never-hungover/nac-and-alcohol) explains what's known and what isn't. If the compound is actually acetyl-L-carnitine, there's even less hangover-specific research to point to.

### Vitamin C and B vitamins

There's no good evidence that taking vitamin C or B vitamins the night you drink prevents a hangover. People who drink heavily over time can run low on some B vitamins, especially thiamine, and that matters for long-term health. But for a social drinker who eats a normal diet, topping up B vitamins before bed is unlikely to change how you feel the next morning. These ingredients are low risk and cheap, which is why nearly every hangover product includes them.

### What the bigger reviews say

Independent reviews of hangover remedies as a whole are not encouraging. A 2005 systematic review in the *BMJ* by Pittler, Verster, and Ernst found no compelling evidence that any conventional or complementary remedy prevents or treats hangover. A larger 2022 review in the journal *Addiction* reached a similar conclusion: the studies that exist are small and of very low quality, and none of them justify confident claims. DHM-based products, Sobur included, fall into that same picture.

### The "clinically proven" and "cure" claims

Sobur's marketing describes its ingredients as clinically proven and the product as a hangover cure. Based on the evidence above, neither claim holds up. The science page lists references, but they mostly cover how alcohol affects the body (absorption, flushing, GABA, vasopressin) rather than trials of the product. In 2020, the FDA sent warning letters to several companies for marketing dietary supplements as hangover cures or preventives, because a supplement making those claims is being sold like an unapproved drug. We're not saying Sobur received one of those letters. We're saying the "cure" language is the kind regulators object to, and it's a reason to read the rest of the marketing with some skepticism.

### What Sobur can't do

Like every hangover supplement, Sobur does not:

- Lower your blood alcohol or sober you up faster in any way you'd notice.
- Make it safe to drive, swim, or make important decisions after drinking.
- Undo dehydration, poor sleep, or the effects of drinking on an empty stomach.
- Protect you from the long-term effects of heavy or frequent drinking.

If you're expecting it to let you drink more without consequences, you'll be disappointed, and you could put yourself at risk.

## Sobur Side Effects and Safety

### Possible side effects

Sobur's short ingredient list is a plus here: fewer ingredients means fewer things that can disagree with you. Most people who take DHM, NAC, vitamin C, and B vitamins at these kinds of doses report no side effects. When people do notice something, it's usually:

- **Stomach upset or nausea,** more likely on an empty stomach. NAC in particular can cause mild nausea in some people.
- **Headache or drowsiness,** which can be hard to separate from the drinking itself.
- **Flushing or a warm feeling,** sometimes reported with niacin (vitamin B3) at higher doses.

### Medication interactions

This is the area to take seriously. DHM's long-term safety in people hasn't been studied well, and lab research suggests it may affect some liver enzymes that process medicines. Because DHM acts on GABA receptors, there's a theoretical concern about combining it with sedatives, sleep aids, or anti-anxiety medicines. NAC can affect blood clotting at high doses and may interact with nitroglycerin and some blood pressure medicines. Our [DHM medication interactions guide](/never-hungover/dhm-medication-interactions-safety-guide-2025) covers this in more detail.

The practical rule: if you take any prescription medicine regularly, show the Sobur label to a pharmacist before you try it. That takes two minutes and is free.

### Who should avoid it or ask first

- People who are pregnant or breastfeeding (there's no safety data).
- People with liver or kidney disease.
- People taking blood thinners, sedatives, sleep medicines, anxiety medicines, or diabetes medicines.
- Anyone under the legal drinking age.

## Sobur Hangover Pills: Where to Buy and What It Costs

Sobur is mainly sold through its own website, which advertises flat-rate shipping and a money-back guarantee. It has also appeared on Amazon and on marketplaces in Southeast Asia under listings like "Sobur Hangover Support, 20 Capsules." Availability on third-party sites comes and goes, so if you buy outside the brand's own store, check the seller and make sure the packaging matches the brand's current product.

We don't quote exact prices because they change and vary by seller and country. The useful way to judge value is the per-serving math from earlier. Because the bottles are small and the DHM dose is modest, Sobur generally works out more expensive per milligram of DHM than plain DHM products. If you value the convenience of NAC and vitamins in the same capsule, that may be worth it to you. If you're paying mainly for DHM, it usually isn't.

On the money-back guarantee: these offers are worth something, but read the terms first. Some only apply to unopened bottles, or require you to request the refund within a set window.

## What Users Say About Sobur

Sobur has far fewer reviews than the big DHM brands, so there's less to go on. The reviews that exist follow the pattern we see across hangover supplements. Reviews aren't clinical evidence, and people with strong reactions either way are the most likely to write one, but the patterns are still useful.

### What people like

- **"I felt better than usual the next day."** The most common positive comment, usually after a moderate night and plenty of water.
- **Few capsules.** One or two capsules is easier to manage at the end of a night than products that need four or more.
- **A simple label.** Some buyers prefer a short formula they can understand.

### What people complain about

- **No noticeable effect,** especially after heavier nights.
- **Small bottles** that run out quickly if you take two capsules each time.
- **Cost** compared with larger bottles of plain DHM.

The recurring advice from experienced users of hangover supplements in general applies here too: they seem to help most on moderate nights, they work better alongside water, food, and sleep, and they don't rescue a night of very heavy drinking.

## How Sobur Compares With Other Hangover Products

The hangover supplement market splits into a few camps. Here's where Sobur sits:

- **Plain DHM products:** the highest DHM dose for the money and the simplest label. Sobur gives you less DHM but adds NAC and vitamins.
- **DHM-focused blends** such as Cheers Restore and Flyby: DHM plus a handful of supporting ingredients, closer to Sobur's approach but usually with more DHM. See our [Cheers Restore review](/never-hungover/cheers-restore-review) and [Flyby review](/never-hungover/flyby-recovery-review-2025) for the trade-offs.
- **Broad "kitchen sink" formulas** such as AfterDrink: many ingredients, small amounts of each. Our [AfterDrink review](/never-hungover/afterdrink-review) explains why that dilutes each one.
- **Probiotic and enzyme drinks** such as ZBiotics: a different idea entirely, targeting acetaldehyde in the gut.

For a broader look at whether any of these product types work, see [do hangover pills actually work?](/never-hungover/do-hangover-pills-actually-work), and for a side-by-side of DHM brands, our [best DHM supplements guide](/never-hungover/best-dhm-supplements).

## How to Use Sobur (If You Try It)

If you decide to try Sobur, a few habits make it more likely you'll get any benefit and less likely you'll have a problem:

1. **Read the Supplement Facts panel first.** Confirm the serving size, the DHM amount per serving, and whether the "NAC" is N-acetyl cysteine.
2. **Follow the label.** The brand suggests one to two capsules before bed with plenty of water. Don't take extra to make up for a heavier night.
3. **Drink water through the evening, not just at the end.** Alternating alcoholic drinks with water does more than any capsule.
4. **Eat before and while you drink.** Food in your stomach slows how fast alcohol reaches your bloodstream.
5. **Protect your sleep.** Poor sleep is a big part of why the next day feels bad.
6. **Try it on a normal night first,** not before a big event, so you know how your stomach handles it.

## Pros and Cons Summary

**Pros**

- Short, understandable formula built around DHM.
- Only one to two capsules per serving.
- Includes NAC, vitamin C, and B vitamins in the same capsule.
- Long-running brand with a stated money-back guarantee.

**Cons**

- The advertised 300 mg of DHM is low next to most DHM products.
- Small bottles and modest dose make it expensive per milligram of DHM.
- Marketing uses "cure" and "clinically proven" language the evidence doesn't support.
- An apparent labeling inconsistency about which "NAC" compound is included.
- No published third-party testing we could find, and no trial of the product itself.

## The Bottom Line

Sobur is a reasonable, simple product with an honest-looking ingredient list and a marketing department that overpromises. If you like the idea of DHM plus NAC and vitamins in one or two capsules, it's a legitimate option to try on a moderate night, as long as you check the label and clear it with a pharmacist if you take other medicines. If what you want is DHM itself, you'll get more of it for less money elsewhere.

*Disclosure: the two links below are Amazon affiliate links. We earn a small commission if you buy through them, at no extra cost to you.*

If DHM is the ingredient you're after, these are two standalone options we've reviewed:

- [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20): about 1,000 mg of DHM per serving and one of the lowest costs per serving we've found. A simple, single-ingredient option.
- [No Days Wasted DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20): about 1,000 mg of DHM plus L-cysteine and a few supporting ingredients, so it's the closest match to Sobur's "DHM plus support" idea, at a higher DHM dose. It costs more per serving than Double Wood.

Neither is a hangover cure either. There is no good evidence that any supplement prevents hangovers reliably. They simply give you more of the ingredient most people are paying for. You can compare more options on our [supplement reviews page](/reviews).

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Does Sobur actually work?**

It may help some people feel a little better after a moderate night, but there's no independent clinical trial of Sobur itself. Its main ingredient, DHM, has promising animal research and limited human data, and the advertised 300 mg dose is on the low side. There is no good evidence that Sobur or any other supplement prevents hangovers reliably.

**Is Sobur legit?**

Sobur appears to be a real, long-running product from a small company (Fortius Labs LTD) with a straightforward DHM-based formula. The product itself seems legitimate. The marketing is the weak part: calling it a "hangover cure" and its ingredients "clinically proven" goes well beyond what the evidence shows.

**How many Sobur pills should I take?**

The brand suggests one to two capsules before bed with plenty of water. Check the Supplement Facts panel to see whether the DHM amount is listed per capsule or per two-capsule serving, and don't go above the label directions.

**Does Sobur have side effects?**

Most people report none. Possible side effects include mild stomach upset or nausea (more likely on an empty stomach), headache, drowsiness, or flushing from niacin. Because DHM and NAC can interact with some medicines, ask a pharmacist first if you take blood thinners, sedatives, sleep aids, anxiety medicine, or other prescriptions.

**How much DHM is in Sobur?**

Sobur's long-running Amazon listing advertises 300 mg of DHM. That's at the low end of the 300 to 1,200 mg range people commonly use, and well below the roughly 1,000 mg in most plain DHM products.

**Is Sobur better than Cheers or plain DHM?**

Not on DHM dose or value. Plain DHM products usually give you about three times as much DHM for less money, and DHM blends like Cheers Restore also tend to provide more. Sobur's advantage is a short formula that adds NAC, vitamin C, and B vitamins in one or two capsules.

**Can I drive after taking Sobur?**

No. Sobur does not lower your blood alcohol or sober you up. If you've been drinking, don't drive, regardless of any supplement you've taken.
